Definition: to be (causatively, do or declare) wrong; by implication, to disturb, violate
BiblicalUsage: Rasha' is to be wicked, to do or declare wrong. Solomon prayed that if Israel sinned and returned, saying, 'We have sinned, and have done perversely, we have committed wickedness'; Daniel confessed, 'We have sinned, and have committed iniquity, and have done wickedly, and have rebelled'; and Nehemiah says, 'Howbeit thou art just in all that is brought upon us; for thou hast done right, but we have done wickedly.'
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the confession is the same in every age: we have done wickedly, and Thou art just. And I hold that the prayer only works because the confession is honest — Solomon, Daniel, and Nehemiah all say the same words, and God hears them all.
